short: Choiceless polynomial time is not P

title.title: Choiceless polynomial time does not capture P
title.subtitle: Claim: a polynomial-time query on finite structures that choiceless polynomial time with counting can't define

beats.text: Schematic: properties of unordered finite structures decidable in polynomial time
Choiceless polynomial time with counting (CPT) was the leading candidate to capture them
The claim: solving linear systems over $\mathbb{F}_3$ is in PTIME but not in CPT

achievement.label: Blass–Gurevich–Shelah conjecture (1999)
achievement.context: Before: separations only for restricted variants of CPT (Pakusa, Grädel, Schalthöfer, Lichter)
achievement.note: Not P vs NP, and not whether some other logic captures PTIME

verify.detail: Both separations are in Lean, which has to encode CPT itself
verify.ourCheck: We read the Lean docs and allowed axioms; we did not build it

sources.quote: Blass-Gurevich-Shelah (1999) introduced CPT and conjectured it does not capture PTIME.
Pakusa, Gradel, Schalthofer, Lichter (2021-2023) separated CPT variants
an explicit isomorphism-invariant query on finite structures in an 8-relation vocabulary (consistency of a linear system over F_3) is decidable in polynomial time but not CPT-definable
The separation is unconditional and does not separate P from NP or settle whether some other logic captures PTIME (Gurevich's question). The formal statement defines CPT inside Lean
only `propext`, `Quot.sound` and `Classical.choice` for every family here

plain: A leading candidate 'language' for all fast computations on unordered data misses one fast problem

steps: Build two grid-like structures: total charge zero, or one
Linear equations over $\mathbb{F}_3$ tell them apart in polynomial time
Their symmetries make every CPT program answer alike

voice.text: Choiceless polynomial time with counting was the leading candidate to capture polynomial time.
Two grids differ by one charge; symmetry hides it from every such program.
Claimed: a polynomial time query it cannot define.
